summary: Defines the use case for Infrastructure ENUM and proposes a parallel namespace to e164.arpa as a long-term solution. It would let carriers publish DNS records for telephone numbers independently of those created by the number holders.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo proposes a separate ENUM namespace for carriers to publish records about telephone numbers they serve. Carrier records can be managed independently from records provisioned by end users.

subtitle: A proposal for a carrier-controlled ENUM namespace parallel to e164.arpa.

tldr.problem: The original ENUM model is based on end-user opt-in, while carriers need to provision records for numbers they serve independently of end-user records.
tldr.mechanism: The memo proposes a parallel Infrastructure ENUM namespace in which service providers control Tier 2 records for E.164 numbers they serve.
tldr.outcome: The RFC defines the use case and proposes a namespace parallel to e164.arpa; it says the domain for that namespace is yet to be determined.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 5526 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC proposes a parallel namespace but says its domain is still to be determined.

sections.title: Why Infrastructure ENUM
sections.content:
ENUM maps E.164 telephone numbers to domain names and uses DNS to find NAPTR records describing available services. The original ENUM model was based on end-user opt-in.

The memo says service providers need to provision records for large numbers of allocated or hosted numbers without requiring each user to opt in. Such records can support provider interconnection and number-portability applications.
sections.plainLanguage: ENUM turns a telephone number into a DNS lookup. This proposal addresses carrier records that need to be managed separately from individual users' records.

sections.title: A Parallel Namespace
sections.content:
The memo proposes a namespace parallel to e164.arpa for Infrastructure ENUM, with the domain name still to be determined. A parallel namespace allows carriers and end users to manage their registrations independently.

Infrastructure ENUM Tier 2 records would be controlled by the service provider for the E.164 number, generally called the carrier-of-record. The definition of carrier-of-record is a national matter or is set by the authority controlling the numbering space.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal keeps carrier records in a separate DNS branch. The carrier responsible for a number controls the records beneath that branch.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
The memo says the over-the-network ENUM protocol does not change when a new zone apex is added, so the security considerations of RFC 3761 continue to apply. It refers readers to RFC 5067 for specific Infrastructure ENUM security considerations.

Infrastructure ENUM records should resolve to service-provider points of interconnection rather than end-user equipment. Providers should protect end users from unwanted communications as they do for other interconnections.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposal leaves ENUM's network protocol unchanged. Providers should direct records to their own interconnection points and protect customers from unwanted communication.
